quote: on average across 30 countries, 30% of adults say most people can be trusted. Among these countries, interpersonal trust is highest in China and India, where 56% say most people can be trusted, and lowest in Brazil, Malaysia, and Turkey, where fewer than 15% say so
why: Ipsos confirms the 30% average, the China/India high and the Brazil/Malaysia/Turkey low.

quote: The survey was conducted among 22,534 adults under the age of 75 conducted between February 18 and March 4
why: Sample size, country count and Feb-Mar 2022 timing confirmed in the methodology.

quote: average across 30 countries, 30% of adults say most people can be trusted. Among these countries, interpersonal trust is highest in China and India, where 56% say most people can be trusted, and lowest in Brazil, Malaysia, and Turkey, where fewer than 15% say so
why: Percentages and country extremes match the claim.

quote: The survey was conducted among 22,534 adults under the age of 75 conducted between February 18 and March 4 on Ipsos's Global Advisor online survey platform.
why: Confirms sample size and timing.

quote: 31% expressing a "great deal" or "fair amount" of confidence in the media to report the news "fully, accurately and fairly," similar to last year's 32%. Americans' trust in the media -- such as newspapers, television and radio -- first fell to 32% in 2016
why: Gallup confirms 31% tying the 32% record low first set in 2016.

quote: In three readings in the 1970s, trust ranged from 68% to 72%
why: Confirms trust was roughly 70% in the early 1970s.

quote: For the third consecutive year, more U.S. adults have no trust at all in the media (36%) than trust it a great deal or fair amount.
why: The 36% figure and the third consecutive year are verified.

quote: 85 percent of respondents said that they are "very concerned" or "somewhat concerned" about the spread of misleading video and audio deepfakes.
why: Confirms the August 2023 YouGov finding of 85% concern.

quote: we also originally conjectured that these claims of misinformation could further undermine trust in media, but we generally find no such impacts.
why: Confirms the claims helped politicians but did not significantly reduce media trust.

quote: This study devotes attention to these indirect effects and provides novel experimental evidence related to one such subtle and concerning consequence of misinformation: the liar's dividend.
why: Confirms the paper is an APSR experimental study on the liar's dividend.

quote: To help, we surveyed 20,000 people in 11 countries... 85% of leaders say that the shift to hybrid work has made it challenging to have confidence that employees are being productive
why: Confirms the 20,000 person sample and the 85% figure.

quote: To help, we surveyed 20,000 people in 11 countries and analyzed trillions of Microsoft 365 productivity signals
why: Confirms sample size and scope of the 2022 Work Trend Index.

quote: 85% of leaders say that the shift to hybrid work has made it challenging to have confidence that employees are being productive... This has led to productivity paranoia
why: Confirms the 85% figure and the productivity paranoia phrase.

quote: Nearly half of employed U.S. job seekers (49%) believe artificial intelligence (AI) tools used in job recruiting are more biased than their human counterparts
why: Confirms the 49% figure.

quote: Results for the Bentley-Gallup Business in Society study are based on web survey responses collected May 8-15, 2023, from 5,458 U.S. adults
why: Confirms May 2023 timing and the 5,458 sample.

quote: majorities believe AI performs as well as or better than humans at customizing the content users see online (68%)... About two-thirds of Americans believe AI performs worse than humans on each of these tasks
why: Confirms the 68% and the two-thirds findings.

quote: Results for the Bentley-Gallup Business in Society study are based on web survey responses collected May 8-15, 2023, from 5,458 U.S. adults
why: Confirms May 2023 timing and the 5,458 sample.

quote: For this analysis, we surveyed 11,004 U.S. adults from Dec. 12 to 18, 2022.
why: Confirms the Dec 2022 fieldwork and 11,004 sample.

quote: The Pew Research Center survey, conducted Dec. 12-18, 2022, of 11,004 U.S. adults
why: Confirms the 11,004 sample, though the survey ran Dec 2022 and February 2023 was only the publication date.

quote: our overall conclusion is that trust in implementing institutions appears to have been stable or increasing around the world in recent decades, whereas trust in representative institutions has been declining.
why: Confirms the thousands of surveys since 1958 and the declining representative-institution trend.

quote: a global analysis that collates findings from 3,377 surveys conducted by 50 cross-national and national research projects in 143 countries across the world between 1958 and 2019
why: Confirms the 143 countries and 1958-2019 scope.
